component: P16 offline signature backend, trust metadata, expiry and revocation
constraints: Exact bounded software-statement bytes, one Ed25519 signature, at most 16 provisioned keys and 256 entries per revocation list.
Caller-authenticated policy, expected artifact digest, trusted time and rollback floors; no network, private-key handling or authority grant.
Half-open time intervals, complete key-metadata validation and fixed rejection reasons; optional crypto absence must reject without authentication metadata.
No specified embedded OS, hardware class, throughput, hard deadline or process-memory acceptance budget.
alternatives: CPython validation with cryptography native Ed25519 verification.
Erlang/Elixir OTP crypto and explicit binary/record validation.
Java/Kotlin JCA Ed25519 provider with bounded admission.
Rust ed25519-dalek, including separately specified strict verification semantics.
C or memory-safe bindings to libsodium detached Ed25519.
JavaScript/TypeScript Node crypto with a lexical admission layer.
rationale: KEEP the narrow native verification boundary: raw public-key and signature APIs, explicit dependency-failure mapping and bounded lexical policy validation satisfy the current offline contract without custom cryptographic arithmetic.

Fresh tests exercise expiry/revocation and real dependency absence in normal and optimized isolated interpreters. Six existing primitive cases agree between Python and Node; that is limited interoperability evidence, not full candidate parity.

OTP and JCA are credible managed alternatives but still need application admission and backend availability checks. Dalek strict verification is a potentially different acceptance profile, not a transparent language substitution. Sodium multipart Ed25519ph is not this wire profile.

No material winning migration is evidenced for this constrained contract. Language familiarity, existing code, installed tools and rewrite cost do not justify the decision. Actual native-target requirements or a revised cryptographic profile reopen it.
limits: No universal backend acceptance equivalence, mathematical enrollment validation, live revocation discovery or persisted rollback floors.
Only Python and Node were executed; OTP, JCA, dalek and sodium comparisons are source-based. No controlled comparative benchmark or runtime ranking.
No encryption-at-rest/in-transit, MLS, CNSA, five-nines, hard-real-time, physical qualification or whole-lane completion.
